qAndA.question: What is the chemical formula for ferrous sulfate?
What color is the ferrous sulfate solution before adding zinc metal?

qAndA.answer: They react with the ferrous sulfate, dissolving and forming zinc sulfate.
qAndA.question: What happens to the zinc metal pieces during the reaction?
What is deposited at the bottom of the beaker after the reaction?

qAndA.answer: The reaction between zinc and ferrous sulfate produces zinc sulfate, which has a different color than ferrous sulfate.
qAndA.question: Why does the solution in the left beaker change color after adding zinc?

activities.description: Chemist points to the pale yellow ferrous sulfate solution and adds pieces of zinc metal.
Chemist explains that it will take a little time for the reaction to start.
Scene shifts to two beakers. The left one shows the reaction in progress, with the solution turning a deeper yellow. The right one contains fresh ferrous sulfate solution for comparison.
Chemist explains that the left beaker shows the reaction of ferrous sulfate with zinc.
Chemist removes the zinc metal pieces from the left beaker with tweezers.
Chemist highlights the formation of zinc sulfate solution in the left beaker and the deposition of iron at the bottom.
Chemist explains that this is an example of a displacement reaction, where one metal replaces another.
Chemist shows the iron deposits at the bottom of the beaker.

beaker, sterile and a glass full of water.
First, we will make a solution of ferrous sulphate.
So this plays a few crystals of ferrous sulphate in an empty beaker.
Then add some water to the beaker and stir continuously.
For a little while, you will get a clean solution of ferrous sulphate.
Now this solution will be slightly pale yellow in color.
Now to the solution of ferrous sulphate, we will add a few pieces of zinc metal.
You will have to wait for a while because it will take a little time before the reaction
starts.
Now the left beaker is where the reaction is taking place.
The right hand beaker contains freshly prepared ferrous sulphate solution.
In the left hand beaker, the ferrous sulphate has reacted with zinc.
For a while, you can remove the zinc metal pieces from the left hand beaker with the help
of tweezers.
In the left beaker, zinc sulphate solution will be prepared and iron will be deposited
at the bottom of the beaker.
Now this is an example of a displacement reaction.
We are during a reaction, one metal is replaces another one.
Here you can see iron deposits at the bottom of the beaker.

youtube_description:
Today we will conduct and discuss a Displacement Reaction. For this we will need some crystals of Ferrous Sulfate, pieces of Zinc metal, an empty beaker, stirrer and a glassful of water. We will first make a solution of Ferrous Sulfate. For this place a few crystals of Ferrous Sulfate in the empty beaker. Then add some water to the beaker and stir. After a while you will get a clean solution of Ferrous Sulfate. This solution will be pale yellow in color. To this solution of Ferrous Sulfate we will add a few pieces of Zinc metal. Wait for a while because it will take a while before the reaction starts. 
The left beaker is where the reaction is taking place. The right hand beaker contains freshly prepared Ferrous Sulfate solution. In the left hand beaker the Ferrous Sulfate has reacted with zinc. After a while you can remove the zinc metal pieces from the left beaker with the help of tweezers. In the left beaker Zinc Sulfate solution will be prepared and Iron will be deposited at the bottom of the beaker. This is an example of Displacement Reaction where during a reaction one metal replaces another. Here you can see Iron deposits at the bottom of the beaker.
